Then w1 (the ancestor-of-main job), which is the general-case fix and
needs fetch-depth: 0 plus a merge-base check — model the job on
standard `actions/checkout@v4` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor` patterns

description:
`.github/workflows/release.yml:3-5` triggers the whole workflow on any
`v*` tag push:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
```

There is no job that asserts the tagged commit is actually an ancestor of
`main` before the `build` (line ~52) and `publish` (line ~98) jobs run.
The in-repo comment at the top of the file even documents the assumed
invariant ("the tag fired here has already been CI-validated" via the
`main-release-only` ruleset + squash-merge to `main`), but that invariant
is enforced entirely by out-of-band process (an admin/maintainer only
ever pushing tags after `release-finalize` merges to `main`), not by the
workflow itself. Anyone (or any compromised token) with tag-push
permission on any ref can trigger a real PyPI publish today.

Separately, `workflow_dispatch` (lines 6-13) lets a human manually run the
workflow from *any* ref with `test_pypi` defaulting to `false`. The
`publish` job's real-PyPI step (line 120-125:
`if: github.event.inputs.test_pypi != 'true'`) is gated only on that
boolean input, not on the ref being a tag at all — a manual dispatch from
a branch (e.g. a feature branch) with the default input publishes to real
PyPI. Only the downstream `github-release` job (line ~140:
`if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`) checks the ref shape, and
that's after publish has already happened.

This TODO hardens the workflow itself so the *tooling* enforces the
on-main, validated-tag invariant, not just documented process + trust.

anti_patterns.dont: gate the ancestor-of-main check only on the tag-push trigger
anti_patterns.instead: w1's job must cover both trigger types explicitly, and w2 adds a second independent check on the publish step itself.
anti_patterns.why: workflow_dispatch from an arbitrary branch is the more exploitable gap

anti_patterns.dont: remove or weaken the existing environment: pypi / test-pypi scoping on the publish job
anti_patterns.instead: build on it, don't replace it.
anti_patterns.why: that's the correct mechanism for w4's required-reviewers gate

anti_patterns.dont: try to apply the tag ruleset or environment-reviewer settings directly from a PR
anti_patterns.instead: document the target/live state and let an admin apply it out of band, same as w3/w4 above.
anti_patterns.why: the develop-PR GITHUB_TOKEN has no administration scope (same constraint documented for the existing soundness-path ruleset gap)

work_units.notes:
Add a new job (e.g. `verify-tag-on-main`) at the head of
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, before `dependency-bounds`/`build`.
It should:
  - checkout with `fetch-depth: 0` (need full history for
    merge-base checks)
  - resolve `origin/main`
  - for a tag-push trigger (`github.ref` starts with `refs/tags/v`):
    assert `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tagged-sha> origin/main`
  - for `workflow_dispatch`: assert the dispatched ref/sha is
    `origin/main` itself (or an ancestor of it) — do not allow
    dispatch from an arbitrary branch to reach publish.
Make `build` (and therefore `publish`, `github-release`) declare
`needs: [verify-tag-on-main, dependency-bounds]` (or fold the
assertion into `dependency-bounds` if that's a smaller diff) so a
failing assertion blocks the whole pipeline before any build/publish
work starts.
work_units.summary: Add an ancestor-of-main assertion job that gates build/publish

work_units.notes:
Update the `Publish to PyPI` step's `if:` condition (currently
`github.event.inputs.test_pypi != 'true'` at release.yml:120) to
additionally require `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, e.g.:

  if: github.event.inputs.test_pypi != 'true' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')

This closes the workflow_dispatch-from-a-branch gap independently of
w1 (defense in depth: w1 stops it at the top of the pipeline, w2
stops the specific publish step even if w1 is ever bypassed or
miswired). Confirm the Test PyPI step's condition doesn't need the
same treatment (test-pypi publishes are lower-risk by design, but
note the decision either way).
work_units.summary: Gate the real-PyPI publish step on an actual tag ref, not just the test_pypi input

"### Soundness-path review enforcement (pending admin action)" at

Add a new `### Tag creation restricted to release flow (pending
admin action)` section documenting:
  - target state: a GitHub tag protection ruleset on `v*` restricting
    tag creation to the release automation identity / specific
    actors (not arbitrary collaborators), mirroring how
    `develop-squash-only` restricts branch pushes;
  - the verify command (`gh api repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/rules/tags/...`
    or equivalent tag-ruleset read endpoint);
  - live state at time of writing (no tag ruleset configured, so any
    actor with push access can create a `v*` tag today);
  - why this can't be applied by the write-task's own PR (no
    `administration` scope), same disclaimer as the existing section.
work_units.summary: Document and apply a tag ruleset restricting v* tag creation
